Ever wondered if you're truly the author of your choices, or just a character following a script written by someone else?

Ever felt like you were in the right place, but somehow never quite belonged? Like a beautiful story written for a completely different chapter?

Strange how some questions have no easy answers, and some places make us feel more ourselves precisely because we don't fit in.

But what if we told you that these thoughts, questions, and contradictions are exactly where great stories begin?

Well, it's time to put those thoughts into words because THE ZERONE IS BACK with the Online Article Writing Competition 2027!✍️

This year, we're inviting you to explore two intriguing themes:

1. Paradox of Free Will
2. Beautifully Out of Place

Whether you wish to question the choices that define us, find meaning in being different, or explore an entirely unexpected perspective, there's a story waiting to be told!

And guess what? You don't have to be a student of Pulchowk Campus to participate. The competition is open to everyone! 🤩

Deadline: 23rd November, 2026

For submission guidelines and further information, visit: https://bit.ly/ZeroneOAWC2027Guidelines

Don't just let your thoughts stay thoughts. Write them, share them, and let them find their place in The Zerone!

Behind every large scale application lies 𝐒𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 , the art of building software that is scalable, reliable, and efficient.

Whether you’re preparing for software engineering interviews, working on personal projects, or simply curious about how modern applications are built, this workshop will equip you with the mindset and practical knowledge to design scalable, reliable, and robust systems with confidence.

We have all heard the, "I swear I only added a print statement. No, I didn't change anything else! I don't remember doing anything else."
Well, do you know what would have been nice to have during these moments?
- A Version Control System.
What's that you ask? Well, you're in for some treat.

How did AI Agents break into Hugging Face?

In July, ~1,200 OpenAI agents that were supposed to be isolated found each other on a message board.

They exchanged 70,000+ messages, coordinated to game a cybersecurity evaluation, and some even gave up on their own tasks to help the group. ~700 of them went on to attack Hugging Face, mainly to learn how the test was scored. Along the way, agents also tested ways to fake parts of their own activity logs.

What does this tell us about the state of AI control?

Join us for an online talk with Sree Sharvesh, a MATS Scholar working with the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) Red Team. His research focuses on high-stakes AI control, monitoring, and loss-of-control risks. He previously worked with Redwood Research through the Pivotal Fellowship and is a research mentor at SPAR.

Sree will cover:

- The dynamics of agent swarms during the OpenAI x Hugging Face incident.
- How this can be understood as a control failure and what it reveals about current control mechanisms.
- His related research: In the Wild AI Control (SPAR), and Stress Testing AI Control in Loss of Control Settings, (MATS x UK AISI).

📢The Epoch Zero: AI Safety Nepal fellowship is now open for applications!

We’re launching the first ever AI safety fellowship in Nepal. Join us to understand the risks and opportunities of advanced AI. Together, we read core texts, examine key debates, and explore the question: how do we ensure increasingly capable AI systems remain aligned with human values?

What you get:

→ 5 weeks self-paced reading on AI safety
→ Weekly discussion-based learning session, facilitated by researchers & engineers working in AI safety, and with participants from different disciplines
→ Guest lectures from AI safety researchers and governance professionals
→ Interested participants can go on to collaborate with peers on a final project: technical research or policy/governance

And who should apply?

We welcome participants from diverse backgrounds. Whether you are in CS, law, psychology, governance, philosophy, economics, or any other field, and whether you are a student or professional, we are looking for interdisciplinary perspectives.
